name: Budgeting for Ductwork Repairs During AC Installation in Older Los Angeles Homes

mainEntity.name: How much extra should I budget for ductwork repairs or replacement during AC installation in an older Los Angeles house?
mainEntity.text: How much extra should I budget for ductwork repairs or replacement during AC installation in an older Los Angeles house?

acceptedAnswer.text: In older Los Angeles homes, the condition of existing ductwork often turns out to be the biggest surprise cost during AC installation. Many attics have undersized, leaky, or poorly insulated ducts that cannot pass required duct leakage tests or meet current energy codes. As a rule of thumb, expect to allocate an extra 20–40% of your AC equipment cost to ductwork repairs, upgrades, or full replacement. For relatively modern, accessible ducts needing only sealing, insulation improvement, and minor resizing, costs are on the lower end. If your ducts are in a tight attic, crawl space, or have extensive kinks and long runs, labor increases quickly. Homes built before certain eras may also have old materials or asbestos-containing components nearby, which require careful handling and can add remediation costs. Because duct condition is hard to assess in a quick walkthrough, ask the installer to include a duct inspection and a “good, better, best” ductwork scope in your estimate. Request separate line items for duct sealing, partial replacement, and full replacement so you can plan contingencies. This way, if inspections or HERS tests show more leakage than allowed, you have already budgeted and prioritized what to upgrade first.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older Los Angeles homes often need duct sealing or replacement during AC installation. A realistic extra budget is 20–40% of the AC equipment cost for duct sealing, resizing, or full replacement, depending on attic access, asbestos, and code upgrades required to pass duct leakage and Title 24 tests.
